title: Tiered stuck-word help: T1 sound-out, T2 model-it, near-miss prompt, WordHelpRecord (Unit 6)
accept: Trigger: struggleDetected or sustained silence on the current word for T1 = 4 s (from the tuning file; per-level timing profiles supported as an injected override) starts Tier 1 — fake-clock tests: silence → Tier 1 fires at exactly T1.

Tier 1 — sound it out: plays the word's phonemes via PhonemeSequencer using recorded human phoneme audio, publishing the help_state highlight index in graphemePhonemeMap order so each grapheme cluster highlights as its phoneme plays — digraphs light as one unit ('sh' together, never s-h); highlight sequence matches graphemePhonemeMap exactly for fixture words including digraph and silent-e cases ('ship', 'cake').

After Tier 1 the child gets T2 = 4 s to say the word: child speaks (tracker accepts) within T2 → NO Tier 2, word accepted as helped(soundOut) — wordHelped emitted; continued silence → Tier 2 at T1 + Tier1-phoneme-duration + T2 (fake-clock assertion of the exact timeline).

Tier 2 — model it: plays the whole recorded word pronunciation, then the recorded 'your turn' prompt line, and accepts the child's repeat; after one more T2 with no repeat, the word is accepted anyway and reading moves on — never hard-blocks (tests for repeat-accepted and timeout-accepted paths, both marked helped(modeled)).
never_blocked_test: no path exists where the child is blocked longer than T1 + Tier1 + T2 + Tier2 + T2 without the story advancing (property-style test over scripted event/timing permutations).

Any word receiving Tier 1 or Tier 2 is recorded in WordHelpRecord with the tier reached (soundOut | modeled) and is marked helped internally with NO visible marker (help_recorder writes rows; a §4.3-style metric query over the fixture rows returns the correct help-rate trajectory — transcribed acceptance).

Near-miss prompt path: on wordAcceptedNearMiss the word still turns green (no helped marking, no WordHelpRecord row unless tiers ran) and the controller plays the brief warm model of the correct word — prompt line + word pronunciation audio ('that's it — cat!'); the child may echo but is not required to: reading continues immediately, the prompt never escalates to Tier 1/2 (tests: audio played, no tier started, no block).
help_given(tier) analytics emission hook is exposed (callback/interface — actual client wiring in reading-screen/app-shell); helped word_read results are distinguishable for §5 analytics.
All audio interactions asserted via FakeAudioService (ducking: help audio ducks ambient/celebration per audio-playback policy — asserted by channel tag).
pinned_design: Unit 6 pinned verbatim: trigger = struggleDetected or sustained silence for T1=4s (tunable; per-level profiles allowed). Tier 1: sound out phonemes with recorded human phoneme audio, highlighting each grapheme cluster per graphemePhonemeMap as its phoneme plays; then T2=4s to say the word. Tier 2: app says the whole word (recorded pronunciation), gently prompts 'your turn' (recorded line), accepts the repeat — or after one more T2, accepts and moves on (never hard-blocks). Helped words: marked helped internally, no visible marker (Unit 1 ratified), recorded in WordHelpRecord with tier reached. Phoneme audio = recorded 44-phoneme set (clean, minimal schwa — Unit 13 brief); sound-out order/grouping from authored graphemePhonemeMap. Near-miss prompt ratified: close-enough acceptance still turns the word green — the child is never told they were wrong — followed by a brief warm model of the correct word the child may echo but need not; reading continues immediately; lighter than Tier 1/2, never escalates; exact prompt copy is authored content (Unit 3) — use fixture refs. Timings/sensitivity/thresholds live only in the tuning file; pilot adjustments touch only that file (R7).
notes: Fully headless: FakeReadingTracker drives events, FakeAudioService verifies audio, fake clock controls T1/T2, in-memory Drift verifies WordHelpRecord. The visual rendering of the grapheme highlight is reading-screen's (it consumes help_state from listening-contracts); this ticket owns producing that state. Near-miss prompt copy and recorded prompt lines are authored/owner content — tests use placeholder refs.
